page.title: Project privacy and limits
page.purpose: Control project-local data egress, aggregate budgets, worker and output defaults before any costly or external task begins.

priorities.statement: See where project media can go.
Set enforceable aggregate limits and understand unknown costs.
Choose supported defaults without triggering work.

states.description: No operation is pending; identify the current task and available next action.
Work is acknowledged and queued or in flight with observed progress or an honest indeterminate state.
A safe retry is actively reconciling or executing without blind duplicate side effects.
Explain the current task, saved revision and next meaningful action.
Name what is loading; retain stable layout and existing local content.
Acknowledge the requested operation once and prevent duplicate costly submissions.
Distinguish local draft changes from durably saved revision; never claim saved early.
Explain local versus remote state and conflict resolution without silently overwriting edits.
Retain usable content and identify the specific information being refreshed.
Explain why there is no content and offer a relevant low-risk first action.
Show which inputs, output or services are available and which remain incomplete.
Show age, affected decisions and explicit refresh; never silently spend on refresh.
Confirm the concrete durable result and offer inspection or the next task.
Associate actionable correction with each invalid field while preserving input.
Explain the failed operation, preserved work and safe next action with diagnostic reference.
Identify the unavailable operation and authority boundary without requesting unrelated access.
Keep supported local work usable; mark online operations unavailable and never auto-submit paid work on reconnect.
Explain whether retry reuses an operation identity, reconciles prior work or starts a newly authorized operation.
Explain exact media/destination and wait for affirmative decision.
A policy requiring hard monetary enforcement cannot run on an unsupported unknown-price route.
Show changed policy separately from last durably saved policy.
Identify requests already transmitted and the limits of cancellation/revocation.

claims.statement: External-media use starts disabled per project and includes remote vision, derived screenshots/text and agent/provider hops, not only raw recordings.
claims.rationale: Unimplemented design intent; runtime bindings, exact state setup, visual evidence and operator review remain required.

claims.statement: Budget and privacy settings are independently enforced on all nested work and are never inferred from account or key availability.
claims.rationale: Unimplemented design intent; runtime bindings, exact state setup, visual evidence and operator review remain required.

x-design.layout: Privacy and data scope first, budgets/funding second, workers/output/retention thereafter; explicit saved state and effect on existing versus future operations.
controls: Default local-only external-media policy; explicit opt-in per project with provider/destination and media classes
Inspect source/derived image, audio, text and vision upload manifest and redactions
Set aggregate nested budget, reservations, per-step caps and behavior when price/enforcement unavailable
Select local CPU/qualified GPU/remote worker with capability and privacy constraints
Set output color/resolution/fps/audio defaults, retention/cache and workspace path
Revoke future external use and inspect in-flight requests that cannot be recalled
details: Privacy opt-in, money cap, selected funding, operator authority and agent grant remain independent.
A parent cap includes child calls/jobs; split operations cannot bypass it.
Revocation stops future sends; already transmitted data cannot be promised erased without provider support.
Defaults affect new snapshots only unless user explicitly migrates a draft; active job recipes remain immutable.
Offline saves remain local with explicit pending synchronization, never queued hidden external work.

x-evidence-policy: No fake selectors, region bindings, setup hooks, captures or attestations. Planned controls are metadata until implemented and grounded.
